text:
sam: Heads-up — p95 east-west latency spike across gpu-pool-usw2 during the 09:00 batch window. Started ~09:03, peak at ~09:05, resolved by ~09:09. Affected ~12 nodes in rack-r7. Symptoms: long RDMA send completions, packet retransmits, and a few pod evictions.

jess: Any obvious trigger? recent deploys/firmware/kernel?

sam: No app deploys in that window. infra changed a kernel on a subset of reserved nodes earlier today (kernel-rollback label removed). Also saw a short BGP flap in the region at 08:58 but looked external.

hiro: Can you paste the error snippets from the NIC/rdma logs?

sam: Sure — pulled from /var/log/kern.log on gpu-node-27: 
```
[mlx5_core 0000:06:00.0] mlx5e: qp 0x1000: send completion timeout
rdma: mlx5: qp 4096 response timeout, counters: tx_in_flight=0, retries=16
NETDEV WATCHDOG: ena0 (mlx5_en): transmit queue 0 timed out
```

leo: That looks like mlx5 QP resp/timeouts. Do we have MTU mismatch between hosts and leaf spines? MTU mismatch often causes excessive fragmentation and rdma failures.

sam: Checked quickly: `ip link show` on nodes shows mtu 9000. Switch config snapshot from earlier shows interface mtu 1500 on leaf-12 for the rack (weird). Not sure when that changed.

jess: Oof — leaf mismatch would totally explain fragmentation/retransmit under high batch traffic. Can someone confirm with `ethtool -k/ethtool -S` and `rdma link`? Also capture pcap on the host RX side.

hiro: Running quick checks now. Commands I used: `ip -s link show eth0`, `ethtool -S ens6f0`, `rdma link show`. On gpu-node-27: 
```
ip mtu: 9000
rdma link: mlx5_0 up port 1 (active)
ethtool -S shows RX errors spiked at 09:05
```
But leaf config shows 1500 on that port.

net-bot: deploy-bot: kernel bump to 6.1.27 rolled to [gpu-node-21..gpu-node-30] at 03:02 (label: kernel-nic-fix).

leo: Two orthogonal problems: 1) MTU mismatch between host and switch. 2) MLX5 RDMA stack is sensitive to fragmented path MTU and can hit QP timeouts rather than TCP retransmits under stress. Fixing MTU should be priority.

tanya: Temporary mitigation — can we force those pods to use TCP (fallback) instead of RDMA for the batch traffic? Also roll nodes out of the scheduling pool for new batch allocations until fixed.

sam: Forcing TCP is possible at the application layer but expensive. Easier immediate step: set CNI policy to prefer host network for batching pods on unaffected racks, and cordon the 12 affected nodes. I've cordoned gpu-node-25 and gpu-node-27 already.

hiro: Captured PCAP on gpu-node-27 at /var/tmp/ew-spike-2012345678.pcap. Quick tshark shows lots of IP fragments and ICMP frag-needed messages around 09:05.

leo: OK — schedule: 1) Network team to set leaf port MTU to 9000 for rack-r7 and verify, 2) verify EOS/firmware didn't change MTU via config push, 3) run `ibv_devinfo -v` + full rdma stress (ibv_rc_pingpong) on a test pair, 4) rollback kernel on the nodes that were bumped if issues persist.

jess: Who's owning network config change? @netops?

sam: Pinged netops and filed ticket NETOPS-4521 with the pcap + logs. Netops acknowledged and will look at leaf-12 config.

net-bot: netops: acknowledged NETOPS-4521, will investigate leaf-12 MTU and switch config drift. ETA 30m.

leo: Also let's add a quick automated check in the health probe: compare host MTU vs switch reported MTU and alert if mismatch. We saw this silently fail and impacted batch window SLAs.

tanya: I'll update runbook with the mitigation steps and mark batch window protected for next 24h (no kernel rollouts during peak windows).

sam: TL;DR: root cause likely MTU drift on leaf port causing fragmentation -> RDMA QP timeouts under high concurrent batch loads. Action items: netops MTU fix, collect more rdma diagnostics, cordon affected nodes, add MTU-drift alert, postpone kernel changes during batch windows. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
